name: Spatial Registration Type
abstract: Pixel coordinate system registration for images and maps. Defines properties: basemap, originX, originY, originZ, coordDef, coordUnits, pixelUnits, pixelScaleX, pixelScaleY, originLocation.
description:
# Spatial Registration Type

Defines the pixel coordinate system registration for spatially registered images and maps. Includes origin coordinates (X, Y, Z), pixel scales, coordinate units, and the coordinate definition type (stage-defined or pixel-defined).

examples.title: Spatial Registration Example
examples.content: Pixel coordinate system registration for a spatially registered image map.

annotatedSchema:
$schema: https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema
title: Spatial Registration Type
description: "The affine transform from an image's pixel coordinates to a coordinate
  reference system defined on the sample -- origin, pixel scales, rotation and axis
  sense -- for spatially registered images and maps.\nMODELLED ON A WORLD FILE, the
  sidecar a GIS writes beside a raster (.tfw, ESRI .wld), whose six parameters are
  exactly an affine transform. In world-file letters:\n\n    x_crs = ada:originX +
  ada:pixelScaleX * col + ada:pixelRotationX * row     (C, A, B)\n    y_crs = ada:originY
  + ada:pixelRotationY * col + ada:pixelScaleY * row     (F, D, E)\n\nDEPARTURES FROM
  THE WORLD-FILE CONVENTION. Three, each of which says more rather than less -- and
  each of which a converter has to handle deliberately, because none is a straight
  copy:\n\n  1. ORIGIN CORNER IS DECLARED, NOT ASSUMED. A world file assumes C,F is
  the centre of the\n     upper-left pixel. Here ada:originLocation states the corner
  (upperLeft, upperRight,\n     lowerLeft, lowerRight, center) and ada:coordDef states
  what the coordinates are measured\n     from. Reading a .tfw therefore means WRITING
  originLocation: upperLeft explicitly; it is\n     not implied.\n\n  2. ada:pixelScaleY
  IS A MAGNITUDE, NOT A SIGNED VALUE. A world file conventionally makes E\n     negative
  to encode the y-axis flip. Here the axis sense is carried by ada:originLocation,\n
  \    so the sign is NOT part of the scale. Importing E means taking its absolute
  value and\n     recording the flip as a corner; exporting means re-applying the
  sign. Copying E straight\n     into ada:pixelScaleY silently halves nothing and
  mirrors everything.\n\n  3. UNITS ARE CARRIED, WHERE A WORLD FILE HAS NONE. ada:pixelUnits
  and ada:coordUnits state\n     both sides of the scale. A world file is unitless
  and takes its units from the raster CRS,\n     so an import has to source them from
  elsewhere and cannot leave them absent -- which is\n     why ada:pixelUnits is in
  the inline required list.\n\nSCALING AND REGISTRATION ARE SEPARABLE, and $defs/Scaling
  below is the half that is meaningful on an UNREGISTERED image: a plain ada:image
  has a pixel size, and ada:pixelScaleX on an ada:EPMAImage is a well-formed statement.
  Registration is the other half -- where the image sits on the sample, and how its
  axes relate to the sample's -- and only a map can assert it. The root schema here
  is scaling PLUS registration and is what the imageMap block references; the image
  block references $defs/Scaling. One property name, two shapes, so a placement path
  through either branch resolves."
type: object
allOf:
- $ref: '#/$defs/Scaling'
properties:
  ada:basemap:
    type: string
    description: link to appropriate basemap image map
    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/basemap
  ada:originX:
    type: number
    description: CRS x of the origin pixel (world-file C). Which pixel that is, is
      stated by ada:originLocation rather than assumed to be the upper-left.
    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/originX
  ada:originY:
    type: number
    description: CRS y of the origin pixel (world-file F).
    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/originY
  ada:originZ:
    type: number
    description: CRS z of the origin pixel, where the registration is to a three-dimensional
      frame. A world file has no equivalent, and a planar thin section does not need
      one.
    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/originZ
  ada:coordDef:
    type: string
    description: Whether coordinates are stage-defined or pixel-defined. If pixel-defined,
      are coordinates from stage, upperleftPixel, or centerPixel.
    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/coordDef
  ada:coordUnits:
    type: string
    description: Units of the CRS coordinates, i.e. of originX/Y/Z. A world file carries
      no units.
    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/coordUnits
  ada:pixelRotationX:
    type: number
    description: 'The x-component of one ROW step (world-file B): how far CRS x moves
      per row, which is zero when the image axes are parallel to the sample axes.
      Non-zero whenever the stage was rotated relative to the sample frame -- the
      case a scale-and-origin model cannot express at all, which is why both off-diagonal
      terms are declared here rather than assumed away.'
    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/pixelRotationX
  ada:pixelRotationY:
    type: number
    description: 'The y-component of one COLUMN step (world-file D): how far CRS y
      moves per column, zero for an axis-aligned image. Optional, and absent means
      zero, so a registration that omits both rotation terms is the axis-aligned case
      -- which is what every record carries today.'
    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/pixelRotationY
  ada:originLocation:
    type: string
    description: 'The location of the origin pixel of an image. Range: upperLeft,
      upperRight, lowerLeft, lowerRight, center'
    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/originLocation
  ada:worldFile:
    type: string
    description: 'Link to an EXTERNAL world file that carries the affine transform,
      instead of stating the six parameters inline -- a .tfw beside a GeoTIFF, an
      ESRI .wld, or any sidecar of that form. Use it when the transform already exists
      as a file the instrument or the processing software wrote: restating those numbers
      by hand is a second copy that can disagree with the first, and the file is the
      authority.

      A record states the transform ONE way or the other, which the anyOf below enforces:
      either the inline parameters (origin, scales, corner, coordinate definition)
      or this reference. Both together is permitted and is not recommended -- nothing
      can adjudicate a disagreement between them, and the inline copy is the one that
      goes stale.

      READ THE DEPARTURES BELOW BEFORE TRUSTING A ROUND TRIP. A world file is not
      quite what this object says, so importing one into the inline terms, or writing
      one out from them, needs the sign and the unit handled deliberately rather than
      copied.'
    x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/worldFile
anyOf:
- title: Inline affine transform
  required:
  - ada:originX
  - ada:originY
  - ada:pixelScaleX
  - ada:pixelScaleY
  - ada:pixelUnits
  - ada:originLocation
  - ada:coordDef
- title: Reference to an external world file
  required:
  - ada:worldFile
$defs:
  Scaling:
    title: Pixel Scaling
    description: 'Pixel size and its units: the half of a spatial registration an
      UNREGISTERED image can state. Nothing is required, because an image may know
      its scale or not, and demanding one would make the property unusable on the
      images that do not -- which is exactly why the image block carried no spatialRegistration
      at all before this split, the only available shape having required an origin,
      a corner and a coordinate definition.'
    type: object
    properties:
      ada:pixelUnits:
        type: string
        description: Units of ada:pixelScaleX/Y, e.g. nm, um, mm. Normalise before
          comparing values.
        x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/pixelUnits
      ada:pixelScaleX:
        type: number
        description: CRS units per column step (world-file A).
        x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/pixelScaleX
      ada:pixelScaleY:
        type: number
        description: CRS units per row step (world-file E). A world file conventionally
          makes this NEGATIVE to encode the y-axis flip; here the sense is carried
          by ada:originLocation, so this is a magnitude.
        x-jsonld-id: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/pixelScaleY
x-jsonld-prefixes:
  ada: https://ada.astromat.org/metadata/
